A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and appendices. Renumbered appendices and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-network experiments in Section 4.3 and MAXCUT and Johnson-Lindenstrauss experiments in Appendices F.2 and G.5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Section 4.3 and Appendices G.2 and H.5.

M1.justification: The derandomization objectives, neural-network architecture, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. The revisions concern mathematical analysis and documentation, without introducing a method component or establishing a change to the implemented procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two-dimensional Gaussian teacher-student task, 15-vertex MAXCUT instance, and JL projection task with 100 samples, input dimension 500, and target dimension 30.

E2.justification: MAXCUT retains the classical randomized comparator and exhaustive-search optimum. JL retains comparisons against average and minimum distortion from 1,000 Gaussian projections. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Training budgets, learning rates, metrics, and testing procedures remain unchanged. Freezing the neural network's second layer was already documented in v1 Appendix E. The newly stated sample count of 50 is a disclosure, not evidence of a changed experiment.

E4.justification: The bias and regularization illustrations in Figures 1–2 and the existing convergence analyses are retained. Neither version adds or removes an ablation, robustness test, sensitivity study, or error analysis relative to the other.

E5.justification: Monte Carlo estimation and the 1,000-trial Gaussian comparison retain their reporting practices. No seed information, repeated-training counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: All seven figure images are identical. Both versions report teacher-direction alignment, MAXCUT convergence to 41 versus a randomized baseline around 36, and near-zero JL distortion versus Gaussian average and minimum distortions around 1 and 0.6.

T1.justification: The risk reformulation corrects the regularizer inside the modified loss from perpendicular to parallel weights in v1 Appendix C/v2 Appendix D. The MAXCUT proof revises its norm target from epsilon to epsilon^(3/2), changes the Gaussian-tail estimate, and changes iteration dependence from epsilon^-4 to epsilon^-5. These are localized revisions to existing derivations; the principal lemma and theorem statements remain.

C1.justification: The introduction removes SGD with random initialization as an explicit example of attaining a second-order stationary point and narrows the almost-sure strict-saddle avoidance statement from GD/SGD to GD. The central structure-discovery, MAXCUT, and JL contribution claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3 and Appendix D explicitly clarify joint stationarity over all parameters and explain restricting attention to the first layer afterward. Section 4.3 adds isolation of first-layer representation learning as a reason for freezing output weights; v1 cited stability. The Gaussian-input and generalization limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix F newly specifies 50 neural-network samples. The advertised code location changes from yorgospantis/StructureDiscovery to TPMT26/StructureDiscovery. Most PGD hyperparameter details moved from the appendix into Section 4.3 rather than being newly supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a focused discussion of Hermite and generative exponents and computational-statistical gaps, citing additional work by Wang, Braun, Damian, Lee, and Chen. The existing positioning remains; several other citation changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, expands stationarity and experimental explanations, and moves neural-network training details into the main text. Existing main-lemma proofs receive a separate Appendix B instead of remaining subsections of Related Work. The overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference headers and heading typography, slightly enlarges Figure 3, and reflows figures and algorithm boxes across pages. All seven plots retain their visual content; no figure or results table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the neural-network risk identity, clarifies stationarity requirements, supplies a missing sample count, and improves organization. These provide limited gains in precision and reproducibility. The MAXCUT proof remains problematic: its revised 2 exp(-1/epsilon^4) tail bound does not follow from the stated squared Frobenius-norm bound below epsilon^3, so the theoretical revision is not a complete repair.
